title: Finding Your Voice: Communal Rhythms and Theater
coreMove: Safe performance gives people a place to move and speak with others; song, role, and ensemble turn private survival into rehearsed agency and durable belonging.

exampleSpecs.audience: Ananya, a teacher using theater after a lunchroom incident
exampleSpecs.stakes: A student froze during a peer insult, and the next adult response will either lecture the class or let them rehearse a different action.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use interactive skits to rehearse choice in a charged social moment.

exampleSpecs.audience: Noa, a producer shaping testimony after violence
exampleSpecs.stakes: The memorial can treat testimony as isolated speech or give the room a communal form for grief.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show communal ceremony regulating collective pain.

exampleSpecs.audience: Emily, a program lead working with foster-care youth
exampleSpecs.stakes: The group can avoid hard scenes and make a talent show, or turn life material into supported performance over time.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the long musical process to turn life stories into shared performance.

exampleSpecs.audience: Gail, a facilitator repairing a first rehearsal
exampleSpecs.stakes: The workshop can become a prestige arts event or a disciplined way to build voice and belonging.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use demanding roles to build voice, memory, discipline, and ensemble belonging.

exampleSpecs.audience: Ling, a program director revising a public gathering
exampleSpecs.stakes: A room full of testimony left people isolated, and the next forum needs a shared way to bear grief.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use communal rhythm to hold public pain.

exampleSpecs.audience: Mireille, a clinical lead replacing a lecture circle
exampleSpecs.stakes: The first activity must invite participation without forcing scared students into premature exposure.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Build from theater-based programs without turning performance into pressure.
